source_refs.note: Exercise 3.3, Question 11: book p. 89-90, 24 questions (integration by parts); answer key p. 301 (printed under 'Exercise 3.5')

blocks.explanation:
Yahan \(\tan^{-1}(e^x)\) ke saath \(e^x\) maujood hai, aur \(e^x\,dx\) bilkul \(d(e^x)\) hai.
Is liye pehle \(t = e^x\) rakhenge; integral \(\int \tan^{-1}t\,dt\) ban jayega.
\(\tan^{-1}t\) akela function hai, to Question 1 wali chaal: \(\tan^{-1}t \cdot 1\), first \(\tan^{-1}t\) aur second 1.
Plan: substitution, parts, phir \(\int \frac{t}{1+t^2}\,dt\) log se, aur aakhir mein wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int e^x\tan^{-1}(e^x)\,dx\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(t = e^x\) rakhenge; phir \(\int \tan^{-1}t\cdot 1\,dt\) parts se.

Substitution
\[t = e^x \Rightarrow dt = e^x\,dx\]
\[= \int \tan^{-1}t\,dt\]
Kyun: \(e^x\,dx\) ki jagah \(dt\) aur \(e^x\) ki jagah \(t\).

Parts: \(\tan^{-1}t \cdot 1\)
\[= t\tan^{-1}t - \int t\cdot\dfrac{1}{1+t^2}\,dt\]
Kyun: \(\tan^{-1}t\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{1+t^2}\) aur 1 ka integral \(t\). Inverse function differentiate ho kar algebraic ban gaya, yahi faida hai.

Log wala integral
\[\int \dfrac{t}{1+t^2}\,dt = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}\,dt\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+t^2)\]
Kyun: upar 2 se zarb aur bahar \(\frac{1}{2}\): ab numerator \(2t\) denominator \(1 + t^2\) ka derivative hai, to jawab log. \(1 + t^2 > 0\), is liye modulus nahi chahiye.

Wapas \(x\) mein
\[= e^x\tan^{-1}(e^x) - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1 + e^{2x}) + c\]
Kyun: \(t = e^x\) aur \(t^2 = (e^x)^2 = e^{2x}\).
Dhyan dein: \((e^x)^2 = e^{2x}\) hai, \(e^{x^2}\) nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ldots) = e^x\tan^{-1}(e^x) + \dfrac{e^{2x}}{1+e^{2x}} - \dfrac{e^{2x}}{1+e^{2x}}\]
\[= e^x\tan^{-1}(e^x)\]
Kyun: product aur chain rule; dono fractions cancel ho gaye aur integrand bacha.
